mission: Can one coherent history or multiple histories be distinguished by physically testable predictions?
phase: Foundational framework and literature mapping in progress

milestones.name: Separate time dilation, backward travel, and branching histories
milestones.acceptance: A sourced definitions paper with no category errors

milestones.name: Formalize single-history and branching models
milestones.acceptance: Explicit assumptions, mathematical commitments, and counterexamples

milestones.name: Grade experimental and theoretical evidence
milestones.acceptance: Every entry has origin, citation, category, uncertainty and discrimination status

milestones.name: Develop discriminating thought and computational experiments
milestones.acceptance: A reproducible model or clear proof of a no-go limitation

milestones.name: Publish versioned synthesis and peer critique
milestones.acceptance: Citable review with open objections and change history

disciplines.name: Physics
disciplines.work: Map closed timelike curves and physically realistic constraints.
disciplines.goal: Distinguish tested relativistic effects, mathematically allowed time loops, and rival quantum interpretations.
disciplines.question: Which original predictions, if any, discriminate a physically realized branching history from a single one?

disciplines.name: Mathematics
disciplines.work: Formalize assumptions; test fixed points and contradictions.
disciplines.goal: State assumptions, paradoxes, fixed-point consistency, and causal graphs precisely.
disciplines.question: Do proposed histories differ mathematically in observable predictions or only in interpretation?

disciplines.name: Quantum computing
disciplines.work: Distinguish laboratory analogs from actual temporal loops.
disciplines.goal: Compare quantum circuits, indefinite causal order and hypothetical closed-timelike-curve models.
disciplines.question: What does an experiment actually measure, versus what a circuit merely simulates?

disciplines.name: AI & computer science
disciplines.work: Build reproducible evidence classification and contradiction audits.
disciplines.goal: Build a reproducible source-provenance graph, inference rules and contradiction audits.
disciplines.question: Can claims and revisions be traced through evidence and causal assumptions without overstating confidence?

disciplines.name: Neuroscience
disciplines.work: Separate subjective temporal experience from spacetime mechanics.
disciplines.goal: Separate human experiences of duration, memory and temporal order from claims about physical spacetime.
disciplines.question: Which findings explain perception without implying altered external chronology?

disciplines.name: Chemistry
disciplines.work: Assess whether large-scale quantum interference informs interpretation tests.
disciplines.goal: Review interference, molecular decoherence and scale-dependent quantum coherence.
disciplines.question: What can molecular interference establish about quantum mechanics, and what remains interpretive?

disciplines.name: Biology
disciplines.work: Evaluate where biological timing is informative or non-discriminating.
disciplines.goal: Study circadian clocks, biological timing and the limits of analogy to relativistic clocks.
disciplines.question: Does a biological clock test spacetime structure or only living systems' timing mechanisms?

disciplines.name: History
disciplines.work: Model counterfactual histories and independent provenance verification.
disciplines.goal: Apply source criticism, counterfactual logic and philosophy of science to historical claims.
disciplines.question: How can a claim about an alternative history be framed without fabricating observations?

disciplines.name: Astronomy
disciplines.work: Review gravitational timing and astrophysical proposals.
disciplines.goal: Study observed cosmic clocks, cosmological models and extreme relativistic predictions.
disciplines.question: What do astronomical observations constrain, and do any discriminate rival history hypotheses?

journal.title: The problem is not the grandfather. It is the meaning of a history.
journal.intro: The grandfather paradox is a warning against combining incompatible assumptions. It is not evidence that the cosmos forks.

sections.heading: Three distinct questions
sections.text: Can a clock traverse time at a different rate? Can a physical observer return to an earlier event? If quantum theory branches, are these branches independent histories? The first is experimentally supported; the others remain open.

sections.heading: An evidence discipline
sections.text: A mathematical solution is not a physical device. A quantum simulation is not a journey to yesterday. A philosophical interpretation is not an observation of parallel timelines.

sections.heading: Our research standard
sections.text: Every claim is connected to a dated source, an evidence category, a relevance judgment and a clearly stated limitation. Only findings that distinguish competing accounts can move an empirical verdict.

programStages.title: Define the question and rules of evidence
programStages.deliverable: A clear distinction among time dilation, backward time travel, and multiple physical histories; a falsifiable claim taxonomy.
programStages.gate: Definitions and limits are explicitly sourced; the Truth Ledger cannot mistake interpretation for observation.

programStages.title: Build the scholarly map and planned reading syllabus
programStages.deliverable: Indexed researchers, books, papers and lectures, assigned to discipline reading queues with recorded depth of study.
programStages.gate: Each planned work has provenance, disciplinary relevance and a transparent reading status.

programStages.title: Read, annotate and critically compare primary works
programStages.deliverable: Section-cited notes describing assumptions, derivations, experiments, limitations and opposing results.
programStages.gate: High-priority works are examined at source level; no abstract is counted as a full reading.

programStages.title: Formalize rival models and their mathematical commitments
programStages.deliverable: Explicit single-history, branching-history and chronology-consistency models, with their different assumptions.
programStages.gate: A comparison matrix identifies genuine predictions versus mathematically equivalent interpretations.

programStages.title: Audit experiments, constraints and proposed discriminators
programStages.deliverable: A graded and reproducible evidence table, including strongest objections and negative findings.
programStages.gate: Every meaningful verdict update has a cited observation and an explicit discrimination argument.

programStages.title: Build transparent simulations and discipline exhibits
programStages.deliverable: Reproducible diagrams, calculations and educational simulations for physics, quantum information and other relevant labs.
programStages.gate: Each demonstration clearly distinguishes a conceptual model from a physical experiment.

programStages.title: Write the interdisciplinary synthesis and provisional verdict
programStages.deliverable: A citable research monograph showing what is supported, unproved, contradicted or currently untestable.
programStages.gate: Readers can trace every major conclusion to reviewed works and follow its revision history.

programStages.title: Invite critique, verify reproducibility and archive the final edition
programStages.deliverable: A public, versioned report with outstanding disagreements, replication materials and a continuing-evidence policy.
programStages.gate: The research can legitimately end inconclusive if no decisive experimental distinction exists; unresolved questions are preserved.
